verdict.rationale: Alloy is API-first, so it can be driven headlessly: a complete OpenAPI 3.0 spec covers sandbox and production bases, an Events API supports real-time programmatic integration, and Portfolio workflows can run on a recurring schedule. Its Sandbox mode lets an integration be tested without vendor charges, but it is a per-request dry-run of vendor calls over a shared production data store, not an isolated CI environment, and there is no CLI or CI-specific guidance. missing for 10: official CLI or CI integration docs, an isolated test environment instead of a dry-run mode over shared data, independent or hands-on evidence of CI use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Alloy serves its complete OpenAPI 3.0.0 document at the docs origin
Sandbox makes no vendor calls, so you can test your integration without incurring additional charges
Alloy's Events API allows you to build a real-time integration for decisioning on suspicious ongoing behavior as soon as it happens.
Workflows can run in real time as part of a Journey evaluating an incoming application, or on a schedule as a Portfolio workflow
